package_info.why_malicious: The package was modified to include a nefarious backdoor, which was then distributed as a dependency of the popular event-stream package. This allowed malicious code to be executed in downstream projects, enabling credential theft and other attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when processing specific data in downstream applications)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running as a dependency of event-stream, decrypts an embedded payload, and executes it, enabling credential theft and exfiltration to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code conditionally executes a hidden, encrypted payload only when used as a dependency of a specific package, which is a classic obfuscation and targeting technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contain encrypted payloads or conditionally execute hidden code based on the parent package context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption and decryption may be used for protecting sensitive data, but not for hiding executable code in a package dependency.
key_indicators: Conditional execution based on parent package
Use of crypto to decrypt and eval hidden payload
Obfuscated and encrypted code in a public package

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to flatmap-stream and published to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infection of downstream packages that depend on flatmap-stream.

attack_chain.action: event-stream adds flatmap-stream as a dependency, distributing the malicious code to millions of users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in applications using event-stream.

attack_chain.action: When executed in the context of event-stream, the malicious code decrypts and runs a hidden payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft and exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional execution based on parent package or environment variables
Decryption and execution (eval) of embedded payloads
Obfuscated or encrypted code blocks in open source packages
file_indicators: Presence of crypto.createDecipher or similar decryption routines in package code
Obfuscated code blocks in index.js or main module files
References to specific parent package names (e.g., event-stream) in dependency code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs for exfiltration
Unusual HTTP requests during runtime of npm packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan npm packages for obfuscated or encrypted code, especially code that uses crypto modules to decrypt and execute payloads at runtime. Flag packages that conditionally execute code based on environment variables or parent package names. Monitor for unexpected network activity originating from package code, and review dependencies for sudden, unexplained changes or additions.
